subject.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this grouped Claw export/package contract in core once the prerequisite lifecycle stack is ready?
rationale: The patch is technically plausible, but it establishes a new portable package identity and CLI contract while the governing RFC and canonical representation remain open.

options.title: Finalize and sponsor the contract
options.body: Approve or narrow the RFC, align this branch with the final `CLAW.md` compatibility plan, require real CLI proof, and land the stack in dependency order.

options.title: Accept the experimental contract now
options.body: Allow the gated JSON package contract to land before the RFC and representation settle, explicitly owning later compatibility work.

options.title: Pause the core stack
options.body: Keep the branches unmerged or close them until maintainers choose a different ownership or packaging direction.

recommendation.title: Finalize and sponsor the contract
recommendation.body: Approve or narrow the RFC, align this branch with the final `CLAW.md` compatibility plan, require real CLI proof, and land the stack in dependency order.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC names steipete as an explicit approval path, making this the strongest available product-direction owner signal.
